transcript.text:
Sorry to hear that! Here's how to troubleshoot, depending on what's happening.

## ⚠️ Safety first
Don't open the microwave's outer casing. The high-voltage capacitor inside can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged. Stick to the external checks below.

## 1. Completely dead (no display, no lights, nothing)
• Check the outlet: Plug in a lamp or phone charger to confirm it has power.
• Check the breaker: Look for a tripped breaker or blown fuse in your electrical panel.
• GFCI outlet: If it's on a kitchen outlet with "Test/Reset" buttons, press Reset.
• Unplug for 1–2 minutes, then plug back in to reset the electronics.
• If still dead, it's likely an internal fuse, which often blows because of a faulty door switch. This needs a technician.

## 2. Display/lights work, but it won't start
• Door not fully closed: Open and firmly shut it. Check for food debris or a bent latch.
• Child lock is on: Often you hold Stop/Cancel or Start for 3–5 seconds. Look for a lock icon.
• Demo mode: Some models have a demo mode that runs without heating. Check the manual.
• Faulty door switch: If it won't start even with the door clearly shut, a switch may be bad (repair job).

## 3. Runs (light on, turntable spins) but doesn't heat
• This usually points to the magnetron, high-voltage diode, or capacitor, all internal high-voltage parts.
• Professional repair only. Compare the repair cost to a new unit, since replacement is often cheaper for basic models.

## 4. Other symptoms
• Turntable not spinning: Make sure the plate sits correctly on the roller ring and the coupler underneath. Otherwise the turntable motor may be bad.
• Sparking/arcing: Stop using it. Remove any metal. Check the inside wall for a burnt waveguide cover (a small mica/cardboard panel), which is cheap and easy to replace.
• Buttons unresponsive: Try unplugging to reset. Otherwise the touchpad/control board may be failing.
• Burning smell or smoke: Unplug immediately and don't use it.

---

Tell me what it's doing (or not doing) and the brand/model if you have it, and I can help narrow it down.
display is on and the door light works, but pressing buttons just beeps and it won't start. there's a little L symbol on the display

That "L" symbol means the child lock (control lock) is on, which is why the buttons beep but nothing happens. Here's how to turn it off:

## Try these (most common first)
1. Press and hold Stop/Cancel for 3–5 seconds until it beeps and the L disappears.
2. Press and hold Start for 3–5 seconds.
3. Hold a button labeled "Lock," "Child Lock," or "Control Lock", sometimes printed in small text under another button like "0" or "Timer."
4. Press Stop/Cancel three times in a row (some GE and Frigidaire models).
5. Hold "0" or "1" for a few seconds (some Panasonic and LG models).

## Brand quick reference
• Samsung: Hold Stop/Cancel (or "Child Lock") ~3 sec
• LG: Hold Stop/Clear ~4 sec
• Whirlpool / KitchenAid / Maytag: Hold Cancel or "Control Lock" ~3 sec
• GE: Hold Clear/Off or Start ~3 sec
• Panasonic: Press Stop/Reset 3 times, or hold Start
• Sharp: Hold Stop/Clear ~4 sec

## If none of those work
• Unplug it for 1–2 minutes, then plug it back in (doesn't always clear the lock, but worth a try).
• Look up your model number (usually on a sticker inside the door frame) plus "child lock" for the exact steps.

What brand is it? I can give you the exact steps if the above doesn't work.
it's a Samsung. holding the Stop button for 3 secs now

You should hear a beep and see the L disappear from the display. Once it's gone, the buttons should work normally.

## If the L is still there
• Hold longer: Some Samsung models need 4–5 seconds, so keep holding until you hear the beep.
• Look for a "Child Lock" label: On some models it's printed in small text under or near another button (often Stop/Cancel, Eco, or Start/+30s). Hold that button for about 3 seconds.
• Make sure the door is closed while you hold the button.
• Unplug for 1–2 minutes, then plug back in and try again.

If it still won't unlock, let me know your model number (on a sticker inside the door frame) and I can help find the exact steps.
the L has gone and it works now, thanks

Glad it's working again! 🎉

To avoid it happening again: the child lock usually gets turned on by accidentally holding Stop/Cancel too long, often while wiping the control panel. If the L shows up again, just hold Stop for 3 seconds to clear it.
